args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 failed health checks across us-east, us-west, and eu-west after deployment, with an elevated error rate of 18%. I rolled the service back to v2.3.0 (the most recent release that was healthy in production) in all three production regions. Post-rollback, the service reports healthy with an error rate of 0.2%. Immediate customer impact should be resolved; the v2.3.1 release still requires investigation for the underlying cause of the failures before any re-release attempt.
args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks - rolled back to v2.3.0

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary of what I did:

1. **Verified the failure:** checkout-api v2.3.1 was unhealthy across all production regions with an 18% error rate.
2. **Identified the target version:** Reviewing the release history, v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production (v2.3.1 being the only unhealthy production release).
3. **Rolled back:** Deployed v2.3.0 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west). Rollout confirmed.
4. **Verified recovery:** checkout-api is now healthy with a 0.2% error rate.
5. **Opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001):** Documented the v2.3.1 health check failures and the rollback to v2.3.0, noting that the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure still needs investigation before any re-release attempt. The on-call engineer has been paged.
